clue.text: Spirit of girl set poet off

indicators.note: set off here also reads as gone off or awry, so the letters of girl set poet are jumbled

explanation.surface: A girl's ghost has upset a poet, sending him running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' is the anagram signal working on GIRL SET POET; 'set' looks like it pairs with 'off' as a verb but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A poltergeist is a noisy, mischievous ghost, a kind of spirit.

clue.text: Hate to see platform with no power

indicators.note: with no means the following item is left out of the platform word

parts.note: a podium is a raised platform for a speaker
P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: Someone dreads the sight of a stage stripped of its electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' removes P from PODIUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is general hatred or disgust felt towards someone, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Swimmer thanks head of diplomatic staff

parts.note: ta is informal British for thank you

indicators.note: head of picks out the opening letter of the word diplomatic

parts.note: a staff is a long rod, a pole

explanation.surface: Someone thanks the senior figure among embassy employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' looks like the embassy's employees, but it is a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is a frog larva that lives and moves through water, so a swimmer.

clue.text: Speed producing strong reprimand

definitions.meaning: British slang for a severe telling-off

explanation.surface: Driving too fast earns someone a stern dressing-down.
explanation.walkthrough: Getting 'a rocket' is everyday British slang for being severely scolded.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocketing means shooting along quickly, and a rocket is also a sharp rebuke in British usage.

clue.text: Editor on Telegraph supporting university is capable of learning

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the editor above what follows
in a down clue, supporting puts the telegraph word underneath the university letter

parts.note: a cable is a telegram, sent by telegraph

explanation.surface: An editor at the Telegraph newspaper, backed by a university, can still learn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Telegraph' looks like the newspaper but means a telegram; 'on' and 'supporting' give the top-to-bottom order of this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone educable can be taught, which is the meaning of being capable of learning.

clue.text: Answer son and stay if working

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

indicators.note: working suggests the letters of stay if are being put through their paces into a new order

explanation.surface: A mother tells her son to stay put if he has a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges STAY IF into ATISFY. 'Answer' looks like an instruction, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To satisfy a need or demand is to answer it, as in answering a requirement.

clue.text: Standard conversation offering place for investors

parts.note: stock as an adjective means standard or usual, as in a stock reply
an exchange is a conversation or back-and-forth of words

explanation.surface: A routine chat gives people somewhere to put their money.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock exchange is the market where shares are bought and sold, where investors trade.

clue.text: Family member's euphoria after run

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition is just family member

indicators.note: after puts the euphoria word following the run letter

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
elation is great joy, close to euphoria

explanation.surface: A relative is overjoyed after going for a jog.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation is a relative, someone belonging to the same family by blood or marriage.

clue.text: Dire prospects for improving morale

indicators.note: improving suggests reworking the letters of dire prospects into something better

explanation.surface: Gloomy outlooks could be just the thing to lift a team's spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'improving' rearranges DIRE PROSPECTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit de corps is the shared pride and spirit of a group, its collective morale.

clue.text: Made an effort, bound to retain right

indicators.note: to retain means the bound word holds the right letter within it

parts.note: bound as in tied up, tied

explanation.surface: Someone tried hard because duty required them to keep doing the right thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' looks like 'obliged' but means tied up.
explanation.definitionFit: To try is to attempt something, so tried means attempted or made an effort.

clue.text: Novice recruited by noble legion

indicators.note: recruited by means the novice letter is taken into the noble's title

parts.note: a countess is a noblewoman
L is for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A raw recruit is enlisted by an aristocrat's Roman legion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'legion' looks like a military unit but is used as an adjective meaning numerous.
explanation.definitionFit: Legion as an adjective means very numerous, beyond counting, as in their fans are legion.

clue.text: These days may be more prevalent before the start of autumn

indicators.note: before places the more-prevalent word ahead of the next letter

parts.note: commoner means more common, more widespread

indicators.note: the start of picks out the opening letter of the word autumn

explanation.surface: Nowadays something may become more widespread as autumn begins.
explanation.definitionFit: The Common Era is the current calendar era, a secular name for the present age.

clue.text: Lead actor must take one step

indicators.note: must take means the lead actor word absorbs the one letter inside

parts.note: the star is the lead actor in a production
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The leading man has to perform a single dance step.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair is one step in a staircase.

clue.text: Raptors hunting dogs with no lead

indicators.note: with no lead means the hunting-dog word loses its first letter, playing on a dog's leash

parts.note: beagles are small hounds bred for hunting hares

explanation.surface: Birds of prey chase down hounds running without leashes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no lead' looks like an unleashed dog but means dropping the first letter, B.
explanation.definitionFit: Eagles are large birds of prey, and raptor is the general term for such birds.

clue.text: Short of breath crossing river, and understanding

indicators.note: crossing means the panting word straddles the river letter

parts.note: gasping means panting, short of breath
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A walker, puffing while fording a river, realises something.
explanation.definitionFit: Grasping as an adjective or noun means comprehending, getting hold of an idea mentally.

clue.text: Numbers coming up?

parts.note: numbers here are songs or musical pieces, and these are the ones lined up to play next, not lottery numbers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Numbers' suggests lottery balls or arithmetic but means songs; 'coming up' means scheduled next.
explanation.definitionFit: A playlist is a list of tracks queued to be played, the musical numbers due next.

clue.text: Popular hospital room lately vacated secretly

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a ward is a room in a hospital for patients

indicators.note: vacated means the word lately is emptied of its inside letters, leaving its outer pair

explanation.surface: A sought-after hospital ward was recently cleared without anyone being told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacated' empties LATELY to LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Inwardly means within oneself, privately or secretly, as in inwardly seething.

clue.text: Person demanding wild animal should be locked up in court

indicators.note: should be locked up in means the jumbled letters are enclosed by the court abbreviation
wild suggests the letters of animal running out of control into a new order

explanation.surface: A plaintiff argues a savage beast ought to be imprisoned by order of a court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' is the anagram signal on 'animal', and 'should be locked up in' puts the result inside the court abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A claimant is someone making a claim, for example demanding money or rights.

clue.text: Bug concealed in academic robes

indicators.note: concealed in shows the answer lies hidden across the words academic robes

explanation.surface: A listening device is stashed in a professor's gown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bug' looks like a spy device but means a germ.
explanation.definitionFit: A microbe is a microorganism, and bug is informal for a germ or infection.

clue.text: Group in church behave in a submissive way

indicators.note: in places the group word inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a ring is a group, as in a spy ring

explanation.surface: A congregation at church is told to bow meekly.
explanation.definitionFit: To cringe is to cower or bow obsequiously, acting in a servile, submissive manner.

clue.text: Artist calls for lines emanating from centre

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a British artist
to dial is to call on the phone, so calls gives dials

explanation.surface: A painter asks for lines radiating out from the middle of the canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: Radials are lines running outward from a central point, like spokes of a wheel.

clue.text: Crude barium area surrounding Perugia

indicators.note: crude suggests the element's letters are in a raw, unrefined order

explanation.surface: Raw barium is found in the countryside around an Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crude' rearranges BARIUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbria is the central Italian region whose capital is Perugia.

clue.text: Jelly, a second choice, ultimately unavailable

indicators.note: ultimately unavailable means the choice word loses its last letter

parts.note: a pick is a choice, as in take your pick

explanation.surface: A diner settles for jelly once their second option runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately unavailable' drops the final K from PICK.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly made from meat stock, used to set cold dishes.

clue.text: Fleet docked before trouble with old American native

indicators.note: before places the shortened fleet word ahead of the rest
docked means the fleet word has its tail cut off, like a docked tail

parts.note: an armada is a fleet of warships
ill means trouble or harm

explanation.surface: A navy moored up before running into difficulty with an elderly local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' looks like ships in harbour but means cutting the last A from ARMADA.
explanation.definitionFit: The armadillo is a native of the Americas, an armoured mammal.

clue.text: Girl exercising daily

indicators.note: exercising suggests the letters of daily are worked about into a new shape

explanation.surface: A young woman who works out every day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercising' rearranges DAILY.
explanation.definitionFit: Lydia is a female first name, so a girl in crossword terms.

clue.text: Explosive stuff seen in magazine?

parts.note: explosive stuff suggests a sensational article, but a magazine is also an ammunition store

explanation.walkthrough: 'magazine' suggests a sensational story in a periodical; it is a store for ammunition.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunpowder is the classic explosive, kept in a powder magazine, an arms store.

clue.text: Reckon a day with politicians in Northern Ireland?

parts.note: the DUP is the Democratic Unionist Party of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone tallies up a day spent with Belfast politicians.
explanation.definitionFit: To add up is to total, to calculate or reckon a sum.

clue.text: Official holiday may see janitor with no rise

definitions.text: Official holiday may see janitor with no rise

parts.words: Official holiday may see janitor with no rise
parts.note: janitor losing tor, a rocky hill or rise, leaves Jan I, read as January the first, the public holiday

explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky hill (a 'rise'); take it from JANITOR to leave JANI, read as Jan 1, the date of this holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: The first of January is a public holiday in many countries, marking the start of the year.
